component.name: Forager
component.summary: Install and update apps from their forge releases

description.p: Forager tracks apps published on GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg and other Forgejo or Gitea instances, or on any web page that links to its downloads. For each release it picks the file that fits this computer, verifies it, and installs it the way the system expects: deb, rpm and Arch packages through the package manager, Flatpak bundles, AppImages, or tarballs.

ul.li: See every tracked app, what is installed and what is new
See why each file in a release was or was not chosen, and change the choice
Checksums are checked when published; minisign, GPG and GitHub attestations when you give a key
A daily background check with notifications, and automatic updates that need no password
A log of everything installed, updated, removed or failed

description.p: The Flatpak runs the host's package tools through flatpak-spawn and reads and writes your home directory, since installing software for the host is what it is for. It is not sandboxed in any meaningful way.

screenshot.caption: Tracked apps, grouped by what needs attention
An app's page, with every file in the latest release explained
What an update will install, and how it is verified

description.p: Apps installed in several formats at once, such as an rpm and a Flatpak, are tracked in each format and updated in their own format. Installs are looked for on every check, and removing an app asks which installs to uninstall.

Apps installed outside Forager are recognised on Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE and Arch, as system packages or Flatpaks (user or system-wide), and their installed version is read again on every check.
The latest release is the newest one with a file for this system, so repositories that also tag other builds still find their Linux release.
Apps installed as a deb, rpm or Arch package before they were tracked are recognised as installed, instead of being installed again.
First release, with packages for deb, rpm, Arch, Flatpak, AppImage and a tarball.
